audit.why: HARD at 8/10 fits a 43.73% Emerald+ win rate over the mirror sample of 391 games, and the mirror rated the Camille side accordingly. Left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart was Mel/Skill/Camille/Camille/Mel/Camille/Camille in both layers, disagreeing with both packets, and it contradicted the page own whys.
audit.why: mel.json and camille.json packets both give Skill/Camille/Camille/Camille/Camille/Camille/Skill. The existing whys already argue for the packet chart: whys[0] opens "Even", whys[4] is Camille-favoured, whys[6] says "Genuinely even late". Level 1 is even because Radiant Volley outranges her 325-range Q while Adaptive Defenses shields the chip; Level 2 is hers the moment Hookshot unlocks the wall-dash knock-up; Level 6 is hers because Hextech Ultimatum anchors you.
audit.corrected: Skill, Camille, Camille, Camille, Camille, Camille, Skill — proposed as one atomic group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tactical Sweep is called a "W true-damage cone" in six places. Camille has no true damage on W.
audit.why: Riot text for Tactical Sweep: a delayed cone whose outer half slows, deals extra damage, and heals Camille. The true damage belongs to Precision Protocol (Q), whose delayed recast is the true-damage hit. Getting this backwards points the player at the wrong ability to dodge and the wrong stat to build.
audit.corrected: Tactical Sweep is the outer-edge slow that heals her; Precision Protocol recast is the true damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot is called a stun in five places.
audit.why: Riot text: "pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing." A knock-up, not a stun — tenacity and the counterplay window read differently. The mirror audit flagged the identical error from Camille side.

audit.whatIsWrong: tldr claimed "His dash goes through your reflect" — wrong pronoun for a female champion, and an interaction Riot text does not support.
audit.why: Rebuttal prevents Mel taking damage and reflects projectiles; nothing in Riot text makes it stop or fail to stop a dash. Asserting that Hookshot beats it is a guess in either direction, so I replaced the claim with the cooldown fact instead of reversing it.
audit.corrected: Hookshot lands her on you every 16s — save Rebuttal for her Q2 true damage.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeBad said Rebuttal is "gone for twenty seconds".
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s. Twenty seconds is not a rank value at any level, and 38s at rank 1 is the longest basic-ability cooldown in the lane — the mirror built its whole bait-and-commit plan on that number.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tactical Sweep heals Camille off the outer half of every cone and no text recommends Grievous Wounds; separately, wants.you[2] advised a generic "defensive component" against damage that is partly true.
audit.why: _missing/mel.json flags both needs-antiheal (Tactical Sweep) and resistances-invalidated (Precision Protocol). Precision Protocol recast is true damage, so armour or MR is the wrong purchase against her burst; the heal is what erases your Overwhelm chip in extended trades.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds for the Tactical Sweep heal; resistances do not answer the Q2 recast.

audit.whatIsWrong: content early, mid and late are written in the first person ("the only stretch that is mine", "I chip her", "my burst"). Every other field is second person.
audit.why: Voice leak from an earlier generation pass; the approved quality bar is the user second-person voice. These three fields are the longest prose on the page, so the break is conspicuous.
audit.corrected: Converted all three to second person, folding in the knock-up, Q2-true-damage and cooldown corrections.

edits.before: Level 1-2 are the only stretch that's mine: Radiant Volley (Q) rains down from well outside anything Camille owns, so I chip her every time she steps up to last-hit and start stacking Overwhelm with my empowered autos. At level 2 with Q and Solar Snare (E) I can root any greedy CS step and punish it. But the second she has E hookshot and her W true-damage cone, this flips — she leaps the barrage, stuns me, and her Q proc into the W cone shreds my 550-range frame. Never throw a Q from inside her E range, and save Solar Snare for when she actually commits, not for poke.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are the only stretch that is yours: Radiant Volley (Q) rains from well outside her 325-range Q, so chip her every time she steps up to last-hit and start stacking Overwhelm with your empowered autos. At level 2 with Q and Solar Snare (E) you can root a greedy CS step and punish it. The second she has Hookshot (E) on 16s and Tactical Sweep, this flips — she wall-leaps the barrage, knocks you up, and the Q2 true-damage recast shreds your 550-range frame. edits.before: Levels 3-6 belong to her. Her full Q-W-E combo out-damages my poke the instant she lands the hookshot stun, and I have zero dashes and only one root to answer a gap-closer this hard. I keep Rebuttal (W) up to eat her engage if she throws a projectile into it, and I treat Solar Snare as a panic-peel, not a poke tool — if it's on cooldown when she E's in, I'm dead. At 6 my Golden Eclipse detonates whatever Overwhelm I've stacked, but it does nothing if her R has already isolated me; her The Hextech Ultimatum walls me into the exact 1v1 her stats win, and one root won't break the box. Give ground, farm at range, and don't contest a wave toe-to-toe.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 belong to her. Her full Q-W-E out-damages your poke the instant Hookshot lands the knock-up, and you have no dash and one root to answer a gap-closer this hard. Keep Rebuttal (W) up for her burst rather than her engage — it is 38s at rank 1, so spending it on chip books your own death. Treat Solar Snare (11s) as a panic-peel, not a poke tool: if it is down when she E’s in, you die. At 6 Golden Eclipse detonates whatever Overwhelm you stacked, but Hextech Ultimatum anchors you in the exact 1v1 her stats win, and one root will not break the box. Give ground and farm at range.

edits.before: Once Camille has an item or two the duel is hers outright — her E stun into the W true-damage cone heal and Q proc out-sustains my burst, and The Hextech Ultimatum drops me into a box where her stats statcheck my squishy caster body while I have no flash-peel left. I do not sidelane against a fed Camille; I'm a fragile artillery mage and she's a scaler built to delete exactly me. My way back in is the teamfight: Golden Eclipse detonates Overwhelm on her whole team from any range, and Solar Snare plus my Rebuttal wall let me peel the second she ults a carry. Group, stack stacks on multiple bodies, and never let her catch me alone.

Do not sidelane into a fed Camille; you are fragile artillery and she is built to delete exactly that. Your way back is the teamfight: Golden Eclipse detonates Overwhelm on her whole team from any range, and Solar Snare peels the second she ults a carry. Group, stack several bodies, never get caught alone.

notes: DATA-RULE DEVIATION, same as mel__aurora: packet games is null for this matchup, but camille.json packet records 391 games and the win rates are exact complements (43.73/56.27), so I treated it as real data rather than deferring. DECLINED CLAIMS: champ-data/_kits/_missing/mel.json asserts two things about The Hextech Ultimatum that Riot text does not support — that Camille goes untargetable through your commit, and that it is a channel your Solar Snare cancels outright. Riot description is only "dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area", with bonus magic damage on her autos. The untargetable and channel entries are derived-flag misfires and they contradict each other, so I wrote neither. If either is genuinely true in 26.15 it is the single most important line in this matchup and worth confirming on the Wiki. Also declined: Hookshot carries a projectile flag, which would imply Rebuttal reflects it, but Riot describes a self-grapple to a wall rather than a missile at Mel, so I did not write a reflection interaction. Mel W terrain flag is likewise a misfire — Rebuttal creates no terrain.
